# Introduction

This vignette shows how to go from an age-structured stock assessment to a
surplus production model fitted with SPiCT (Pedersen and Berg, 2017), using the
equilibrium reference points of the age-structured model as priors. The steps
are

1. take an `FLStock` (North Sea plaice from `icesdata`);
2. fit a stock-recruitment relationship and build an `FLBRP`
   (`FLRebuild::eql`);
3. convert the `FLBRP` reference points (MSY, $B_{MSY}$, $K$) into
   Pella-Tomlinson parameters ($r$, $n$) and an initial depletion
   $B_0/K$, which are used as SPiCT priors;
4. build the SPiCT input from the `FLStock` catch and a biomass index, and fit;
5. check convergence and diagnostics;
6. compare the SPiCT estimates with the `FLBRP` equivalents;
7. coerce the fit to a `biodyn` object and project recovery at zero catch from
   $0.3B_{MSY}$.

```{r, pkgs}
library(FLCore)
library(FLBRP)
library(mpb)
library(spict)
library(ggplot2)
```

`FLRebuild` and `icesdata` mask several `FLCore` generics (e.g. `fwd`, `msy`,
`bmsy`), so they are not attached and are called with `::`. For the same
reason `FLBRP::refpts` and `mpb::refpts` are used explicitly.

# Stock

```{r, stock}
data(icesdata, package="icesdata")

stk=icesdata[["ple.27.420"]]
stk=window(stk, end=2020)

summary(stk)
```

# Equilibrium reference points

`FLRebuild::eql` fits a Beverton-Holt stock-recruitment relationship
(steepness parameterisation, with a prior on steepness) and returns an
`FLBRP`. `FLRebuild::refptsEB` adds exploitable biomass (`eb`, i.e. biomass
weighted by selectivity) to the standard reference points.

```{r, eql}
eq=FLRebuild::eql(stk, model="bevholtSV")
rf=FLRebuild::refptsEB(eq)

rf[c("virgin", "msy"), c("harvest", "yield", "ssb", "biomass", "eb")]
```

A biomass dynamic model has a single biomass, so we have to choose which
age-structured biomass it represents. Catch is taken from the exploitable
biomass, so exploitable biomass is the natural choice; spawning stock biomass
(`"ssb"`) can be used by changing `quant` below.

```{r, quant}
quant="eb"   # or "ssb"
```

# Priors from the FLBRP

For the Pella-Tomlinson model, surplus production is

$$P(B)=\frac{r}{p}B\left(1-\left(\frac{B}{K}\right)^p\right),$$

with $B_{MSY}/K=(1+p)^{-1/p}$, $MSY=rB_{MSY}/(1+p)$ and
$F_{MSY}=r/(1+p)$. SPiCT uses $n=p+1$ and the same definition of $r$
($r=mn^{n/(n-1)}/K$ in the SPiCT source, where $m$ is MSY), so `biodyn`, `FLRebuild` and
SPiCT share $r$ and $K$, and $n=p+1$.

`spictPriors` uses `FLRebuild::pellatParams`, which solves for $p$ from
$B_{MSY}/K$ and then for $r$ from MSY and $B_{MSY}$. Initial depletion is the
first year biomass divided by $K$. The priors are log-normal; SPiCT takes the
mean and standard deviation on the log scale, so the CVs are converted with
$\sigma=\sqrt{\log(1+CV^2)}$.

```{r, pellat}
cv=c(r=0.3, K=0.5, n=0.3, psi=0.3)
pr=spictPriors(stk, eq, quant, cv)

pt =pr$pars
psi=pr$psi
idx=switch(quant, eb=FLRebuild::ebiomass(stk), ssb=ssb(stk))

pt
pr$table
```

# SPiCT input

SPiCT is fitted to catch and to the biomass index from the `FLStock`. The
index is an output of the age-structured assessment rather than a survey, so
it has almost no observation error; without some information the index
standard deviation (`sdi`) collapses towards zero. A weak prior centred on
0.1 (log-scale SD 0.5) keeps it away from zero.

Values are rescaled to thousand tonnes, which helps the optimiser, and the
Euler time step is set to a quarter of a year to keep the runtime short.

```{r, inp}
scale=1000
yrs  =an(dimnames(catch(stk))$year)

inp=spictInp(stk, eq, quant, scale=scale, dteuler=1/4, cv=cv, sdi=c(0.1, 0.5))
inp$priors[c("logr", "logK", "logn", "logbkfrac", "logsdi")]
```

Only the priors are set; initial values (`inp$ini`) are left to SPiCT. Setting
the initial values to the prior means led to a poorer local optimum in testing.

```{r, plotData, fig.height=5}
plotspict.data(inp)
```

# Fit

```{r, fit}
fit=fit.spict(inp)
fit=calc.process.resid(fit)

fit
```

## Convergence

```{r, convergence}
c(convergence=fit$opt$convergence,
  pdHess     =fit$pdHess,
  finiteSE   =all(is.finite(sqrt(diag(fit$cov.fixed)))))
```

`convergence` should be 0 and the Hessian positive definite.

```{r, plotFit, fig.height=7}
plot(fit)
```

## Prior and posterior

```{r, priors, fig.height=5}
plotspict.priors(fit)
```

## Residuals

One-step-ahead residuals should show no bias, autocorrelation or departure
from normality.

```{r, osa, fig.height=6}
fit=calc.osa.resid(fit)
plotspict.diagnostic(fit)
```

## Retrospective analysis

Five one-year peels; each refit takes a few seconds.

```{r, retro, fig.height=5}
fit=retro(fit, nretroyear=5)
rho=plotspict.retro(fit)
rho
```

# SPiCT compared with the FLBRP

`spictPar` extracts the estimate and CV of a parameter from a SPiCT fit on the
natural scale. The deterministic reference points (`Bmsyd`, `Fmsyd`) are used,
since these correspond to the equilibrium reference points of the `FLBRP`; the
stochastic versions (`Bmsy`, `Fmsy`) also depend on the process error.

```{r, gp}
gp=function(nm, fit, i=1) spictPar(fit, nm, i)
```

The `FLBRP` harvest rate at MSY is $MSY/B_{MSY}$ for the chosen biomass, which
is comparable with the SPiCT $F_{MSY}$; the age-based $F_{bar}$ at MSY is
shown separately. Biomass and catch are in thousand tonnes.

```{r, compare}
tl  =match(max(yrs), fit$inp$time)
bmsy=c(rf["msy", quant])

hrTerm=c(catch(stk)[, ac(max(yrs))])/c(idx[, ac(max(yrs))])

flbrp=c(r       =c(pt["r"]),
        K       =c(pt["k"])/scale,
        n       =c(pt["p"])+1,
        BmsyK   =bmsy/c(pt["k"]),
        MSY     =c(rf["msy", "yield"])/scale,
        Bmsy    =bmsy/scale,
        Fmsy    =c(rf["msy", "yield"])/bmsy,
        BBmsy   =c(idx[, ac(max(yrs))])/bmsy,
        FFmsy   =hrTerm/(c(rf["msy", "yield"])/bmsy))

spct=rbind(r    =gp("logr",     fit),
           K    =gp("logK",     fit),
           n    =gp("logn",     fit),
           BmsyK=c(gp("logBmsyd", fit)[1]/gp("logK", fit)[1], NA),
           MSY  =gp("logm",     fit),
           Bmsy =gp("logBmsyd", fit),
           Fmsy =gp("logFmsyd", fit),
           BBmsy=gp("logBBmsy", fit, tl),
           FFmsy=gp("logFFmsy", fit, tl))

cmp=data.frame(FLBRP     =flbrp,
               SPiCT     =spct[names(flbrp), 1],
               SPiCT.cv  =spct[names(flbrp), 2],
               ratio     =spct[names(flbrp), 1]/flbrp)

knitr::kable(cmp, digits=3,
  caption=paste0("FLBRP (", quant, ") and SPiCT estimates, ",
                 "terminal year ", max(yrs), "."))
```

```{r, fbar}
c(FbarMSY=c(rf["msy", "harvest"]))
```

SPiCT estimates a catchability $q$ for the index, even though the index is
itself a biomass. If $q<1$ SPiCT biomass is larger than the `FLStock`
biomass, so $B/B_{MSY}$ can differ even when the production functions are
similar. Fixing $q=1$ (e.g. a tight prior on `logq`) forces the two biomass
scales to agree.

```{r, q}
gp("logq", fit)
```

# Comparison figures

Three figures compare the age-structured stock (`FLStock` and `FLBRP`) with
SPiCT: the time series, the production functions and the process error.
All biomass and catch values are in thousand tonnes.

`spAnn` extracts a SPiCT quantity at the start of each year, with its 95%
confidence interval.

```{r, spAnn}
ann  =match(yrs, round(fit$inp$time, 6))
spAnn=function(nm) {
  x=get.par(nm, fit, exp=TRUE)[ann, , drop=FALSE]
  data.frame(year=yrs, lower=x[, "ll"], est=x[, "est"], upper=x[, "ul"])}

C     =c(catch(stk))/scale
B     =c(idx)/scale
nY    =length(yrs)
fmsyBR=c(rf["msy", "yield"])/bmsy
clrs  =c(FLStock="grey40", FLBRP="grey40", "Pella-Tomlinson (FLBRP)"="black",
         SPiCT="red")
```

## Trajectories

Biomass and fishing mortality on the absolute scale (top) and relative to each
model's own reference points (bottom). For the `FLStock`, fishing mortality is
the harvest rate (catch divided by the chosen biomass) and $F_{MSY}$ is
$MSY/B_{MSY}$ from the `FLBRP`; SPiCT $F$ is an instantaneous rate, so the two
are only approximately comparable on the absolute scale. Shaded areas are the
SPiCT 95% confidence intervals.

```{r, trajectories, fig.height=6}
pnl=c("Biomass (kt)", "F or harvest rate", "B/BMSY", "F/FMSY")
fls=data.frame(year=yrs, lower=NA, upper=NA, source="FLStock")

trj=rbind(cbind(fls, est=B,               panel=pnl[1]),
          cbind(fls, est=C/B,             panel=pnl[2]),
          cbind(fls, est=B*scale/bmsy,    panel=pnl[3]),
          cbind(fls, est=C/B/fmsyBR,      panel=pnl[4]),
          cbind(spAnn("logB"),     source="SPiCT", panel=pnl[1]),
          cbind(spAnn("logFs"),    source="SPiCT", panel=pnl[2]),
          cbind(spAnn("logBBmsy"), source="SPiCT", panel=pnl[3]),
          cbind(spAnn("logFFmsy"), source="SPiCT", panel=pnl[4]))
trj$panel=factor(trj$panel, levels=pnl)

ggplot(trj, aes(year, est, colour=source))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower, ymax=upper, fill=source),
              data=subset(trj, source=="SPiCT"), alpha=0.2, colour=NA,
              show.legend=FALSE)+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=1), data=data.frame(panel=factor(pnl[3:4], levels=pnl)),
             linetype=2)+
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales="free_y")+
  scale_colour_manual(values=clrs)+scale_fill_manual(values=clrs, guide="none")+
  expand_limits(y=0)+
  labs(x="Year", y="", colour="")+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
```

## Production functions

The `FLBRP` equilibrium curve is obtained by evaluating the `FLBRP` over a
range of $F_{bar}$ and plotting equilibrium yield against the chosen biomass.
It is compared with the Pella-Tomlinson curve fitted to it
(`FLRebuild::pellatParams`, used as the SPiCT prior) and with the SPiCT
surplus production curve
$P(B)=\gamma m\left(B/K-(B/K)^n\right)$, $\gamma=n^{n/(n-1)}/(n-1)$.
Points are the annual surplus production $B_{t+1}-B_t+C_t$ calculated from
the `FLStock` biomass and from the SPiCT biomass. Large symbols mark
($B_{MSY}$, MSY) for each model.

```{r, production, fig.height=5}
eqp=eq
fbar(eqp)=FLQuant(seq(0, 5*c(rf["msy", "harvest"]), length.out=101))
eqB=switch(quant, eb=FLRebuild::ebiomass(eqp), ssb=ssb(eqp))

n=gp("logn", fit)[1]
K=gp("logK", fit)[1]
m=gp("logm", fit)[1]
pSP=function(B) n^(n/(n-1))/(n-1)*m*(B/K-(B/K)^n)

pBR=function(B, r=c(pt["r"]), k=c(pt["k"])/scale, p=c(pt["p"])) r/p*B*(1-(B/k)^p)

bGrid=seq(0, max(K, c(pt["k"])/scale), length.out=201)
crv=rbind(data.frame(biomass=c(eqB)/scale, yield=c(catch(eqp))/scale, source="FLBRP"),
          data.frame(biomass=bGrid, yield=pBR(bGrid), source="Pella-Tomlinson (FLBRP)"),
          data.frame(biomass=bGrid, yield=pSP(bGrid), source="SPiCT"))
crv=subset(crv, yield>=0)

spB=spAnn("logB")$est
obs=rbind(data.frame(biomass=B[-nY],   yield=diff(B)+C[-nY],   source="FLStock"),
          data.frame(biomass=spB[-nY], yield=diff(spB)+C[-nY], source="SPiCT"))

ref=data.frame(biomass=c(bmsy/scale, gp("logBmsyd", fit)[1]),
               yield  =c(c(rf["msy", "yield"])/scale, m),
               source =c("FLBRP", "SPiCT"))

ggplot(crv, aes(biomass, yield, colour=source))+
  geom_point(data=obs, alpha=0.5, size=1)+
  geom_line(aes(linetype=source))+
  geom_point(data=ref, size=4, shape=18)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, colour="grey70")+
  scale_colour_manual(values=clrs)+
  scale_linetype_manual(values=c(FLBRP=1, "Pella-Tomlinson (FLBRP)"=2, SPiCT=1),
                        guide="none")+
  labs(x=paste0("Biomass (", quant, ", kt)"), y="Surplus production (kt)",
       colour="", caption="Dashed: Pella-Tomlinson fitted to the FLBRP (SPiCT prior)")+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
```

## Process error

Process error is summarised with the four-panel diagnostic used at the ICES
SPiCT benchmark (WKBMSYSPiCT4): residuals over time, residuals against
biomass, their autocorrelation, and their distribution. Following Walters et
al. (2008), the realised surplus production $SP_t=B_{t+1}-B_t+C_t$ is compared
with the production function $P(B_t)$. If $P(B)$ is correctly specified the
residuals are white noise around zero; trends, dependence on biomass or
autocorrelation show that process error is absorbing misspecification or
non-stationary productivity.

For SPiCT the residuals are its own process residuals (`calc.process.resid`,
computed after the fit). These are standardised Euler-step residuals averaged
within each year, so they are multiplied by $\sigma_B/\sqrt{\Delta t}$ to give
annual log deviations, comparable with the estimated `sdb` ($\sigma_B$). For the
age-structured stock the residual is the log deviation of the `FLStock`
biomass from a one-year Pella-Tomlinson step with the `FLBRP`-derived
parameters, $\log\left(B_{t+1}/(B_t+P(B_t)-C_t)\right)$. Residuals are
indexed by the start year $t$ of each interval.

`spictPrd` returns the SPiCT production curve and annual residuals,
`prdResid` the residuals for a biomass and catch series and a production
function, and `plotPE` draws the four panels.

```{r, processError, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
sdb=gp("logsdb", fit)[1]

peSP=spictPrd(fit)$traj
peBR=prdResid(B, C, yrs, pBR)
pe  =rbind(cbind(peBR[, c("year", "b", "rsdl")], source="FLStock"),
           cbind(peSP[, c("year", "b", "rsdl")], source="SPiCT"))

peSD=sapply(split(pe$rsdl, pe$source), sd, na.rm=TRUE)
peAC=sapply(split(pe$rsdl, pe$source), function(x) acf(x, plot=FALSE, na.action=na.pass)$acf[2])

plotPE(pe, clrs[c("FLStock", "SPiCT")])+
  patchwork::plot_annotation(subtitle=sprintf(
    "SD: FLStock %.3f, SPiCT %.3f; SPiCT sdb %.3f. Lag-1 ACF: FLStock %.2f, SPiCT %.2f",
    peSD["FLStock"], peSD["SPiCT"], sdb, peAC["FLStock"], peAC["SPiCT"]))
```

# Coercing to biodyn

`spict2biodyn` copies $r$, $K$, $p=n-1$ and $B_0/K$ into the `biodyn`
parameters, and the catch, index and SPiCT annual biomass into the
corresponding slots, rescaling back to tonnes.

```{r, spict2biodyn}
bd=spict2biodyn(fit, scale)

params(bd)
mpb::refpts(bd)
```

`mpb::refpts` gives the same $F_{MSY}$, $B_{MSY}$ and MSY as the
deterministic SPiCT reference points (to rounding).

```{r, plotBiodyn, fig.height=5}
plot(bd)
```

# Recovery from 0.3BMSY at zero catch

To link the production function to rebuilding time, both the SPiCT and the
FLBRP-derived Pella-Tomlinson parameters are projected from
$0.3B_{MSY}$ with no catch. `biodyn` is a discrete annual model whereas
SPiCT is in continuous time, so recovery times for the same parameters can
differ slightly.

```{r, recover}
rcv=rbind(cbind(model="SPiCT", recoverBD(params(bd))),
          cbind(model="FLBRP", recoverBD(FLPar(r=c(pt["r"]), k=c(pt["k"]), p=c(pt["p"])))))

tRecover=sapply(split(rcv, rcv$model), function(x) min(x$year[x$BBmsy>=1]))
tRecover
```

```{r, plotRecover}
ggplot(rcv, aes(year, BBmsy, colour=model))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=tRecover, linetype=3, colour=c("grey40", "red"))+
  scale_colour_manual(values=c(FLBRP="grey40", SPiCT="red"))+
  labs(x="Years since start of recovery", y=expression(B/B[MSY]), colour="")+
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0, 30))+
  theme_bw()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
```

Time to recover depends on both $r$ and the shape. With no catch the
per-capita growth rate is $(r/p)(1-(B/K)^p)$, which tends to $r/p$ as
$B\rightarrow 0$; for $p<1$ (i.e. $B_{MSY}/K<0.5$) this is much larger than
$r$. A lower $r$, or a larger $p$, therefore means a longer rebuilding time.

# Notes

* The index here is an assessment output, so this is a consistency check
  between the age-structured and biomass dynamic models rather than an
  independent assessment. Survey indices can be added as further elements of
  `inp$obsI` and `inp$timeI`.
* Setting `quant="ssb"` gives a much lower $n$ (a $B_{MSY}/K$ around 0.25
  for plaice), since recruitment compensation acts on spawning biomass.
* The FLBRP depends on the stock-recruitment relationship and its steepness
  prior in `FLRebuild::eql`; different choices give different priors.
